     6	/-!
     7	# The Pauli basis test
     8	
     9	This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
    10	conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
    11	Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
    12	`Soundness.lean`.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:admissible`, `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
    17	and `def:pauli-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-367`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is `def:admissible` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    36	-/
    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	
    45	/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
    46	the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    49	-/
    50	theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
    51	  sorry
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
    54	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    55	quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
    56	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
    62	a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
    63	hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
    64	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    66	-/
    67	def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    68	  q := P.q
    69	  m := P.m
    70	  d := P.d
    71	  k := 1
    72	  hm := P.one_le_m
    73	  hd := P.hd
    74	  hk := by decide
    75	  hq := P.hq
    76	  hdvd := P.hdvd
    77	
    78	/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter package.  It is
    79	the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
    80	`def:admissible`, blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    83	-/
    84	abbrev PauliScalar (P : AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K
    85	
    86	/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
    87	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
    88	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
    89	-/
    90	inductive PauliType where
    91	  | point (W : PauliKind)
    92	  | aline (W : PauliKind)
    93	  | dline (W : PauliKind)
    94	  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
    95	  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
    96	  | pair
    97	  | ms (t : MsType)
    98	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    99	
   100	/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the
   101	coordinates displayed in `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   102	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   104	-/
   105	abbrev PauliIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   106	  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)
   107	
   108	/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   109	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   110	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   111	-/
   112	abbrev PauliSpace (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliIndex P → PauliScalar P
   113	
   114	/-- The coefficient register indexed by the Boolean cube in
   115	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.
   117	-/
   118	abbrev PauliRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) := Cube P.m → PauliScalar P
   119	
   120	/- The nested sum is the fixed register order
   121	`V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
   122	/-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   123	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   124	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
   125	def pauliXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   126	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))
   127	
   128	/-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   129	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   130	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   131	-/
   132	def pauliZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   133	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))))
   134	
   135	/-- The scalar block `V_I` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   136	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   137	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   138	-/
   139	def pauliScalarBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   140	  z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ()))))
   141	
   142	/-- The direction block `V_V` of an ambient Pauli vector in
   143	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   144	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   145	-/
   146	def pauliDirectionBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   147	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))
   148	
   149	/-- The `r_X` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   150	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   151	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   152	-/
   153	def pauliRXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   154	  z (.inl (.inr ()))
   155	
   156	/-- The `r_Z` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
   157	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   158	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   159	-/
   160	def pauliRZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
   161	  z (.inr ())
   162	
   163	/-- Select the basis-dependent point block from a Pauli question content in
   164	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
   165	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   166	-/
   167	def pauliPointBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   168	    Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   169	  match W with
   170	  | .X => pauliXBlock z
   171	  | .Z => pauliZBlock z
   172	
   173	/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli
   174	vector.  Lean-only coordinate plumbing for `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   175	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   177	-/
   178	def pauliToLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   179	    LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
   180	  fun i => match i with
   181	  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
   182	  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
   183	  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j
   184	
   185	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   186	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing
   187	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   188	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   189	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   190	-/
   191	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   192	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
   193	  fun i => match i with
   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   195	      match W with
   196	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   197	      | .Z => 0
   198	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   199	      match W with
   200	      | .X => 0
   201	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   202	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   203	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   204	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   205	  | .inr _ => 0
   206	
   207	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
   208	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper
   209	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   210	-/
   211	def pauliSharedProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
   212	  fun i => match i with
   213	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
   214	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
   215	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   216	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   217	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   218	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())
   219	
   220	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   221	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   222	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   223	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   224	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   225	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   226	-/
   227	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   228	  | .point _ => 1
   229	  | .aline _ => 2
   230	  | .dline _ => 3
   231	  | .pauli _ => 0
   232	  | .pairW _ => 1
   233	  | .pair => 1
   234	  | .ms _ => 1
   235	
   236	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   237	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   238	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   239	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   240	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   241	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   242	-/
   243	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   244	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   245	  match t with
   246	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   247	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   248	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   249	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   250	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   251	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   252	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   253	
   254	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   255	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   256	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   258	-/
   259	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   260	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   261	  sorry
   262	
   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=

40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/

     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	
     6	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live

     8	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
     9	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    30	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    31	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    32	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    33	-/
    34	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    35	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    36	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    37	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    38	
    39	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    40	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    41	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    42	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    47	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    48	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    49	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    50	  U * M * Uᴴ
    51	
    52	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    53	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    54	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),

# Local operations — operator guide

This directory is the operative workflow of the repository: the local
replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and
invariants: [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md). Protocol changes: follow
[`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md).

## The lifecycle at a glance

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
```

1. **File an issue**: `local/bin/issue_new.py --title "..." --body-file b.md --label ...` opens
   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
   sub-issue. The brief for it goes in `local/briefs/`.
2. **Open a PR**: create branch `issue-<number>-slug`, worktree under
   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),
   which pushes the branch and opens the GitHub PR.
3. **Dispatch agents**: only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover
   --issue NNNN --worktree .worktrees/<name> -- "task"`. Session telemetry
   lands in `results/telemetry/`.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

## Ground rules for agents

- Read `AGENTS.md` first; the faithfulness policy and proof-integrity
  blockers are unchanged from the parent project.
- Never run `lake update`. Never write to the hot cache. Full `lake build`
  goes through the machine-wide lock (`warm-worktree.sh`/`ci.sh` handle it).
- One session never reviews its own diff.
- Sessions are dispatched, resumed, and archived only via `dispatch.sh`.
- Invoke workflow tools through the primary checkout's path
  (`/…/MIPStarRE-dev/local/bin/…`), never through a worktree's copy — a
  branch's copy can predate protocol fixes (EVOLUTION.md, 2026-08-30).
- Friction with any protocol → log it in `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  propose amendments per `protocols/meta.md`.

# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache

Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:

| script | role |
|---|---|
| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |

Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
`DESIGN.md` wins.

---

## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way

The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
failure. The load-bearing citations:

| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |

The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
build tree.

---

## 2. The two-tier split

`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
parent's failure.

**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
copy.

**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally the same holds:
**every worktree runs its own `lake exe cache get`.**

> **Tier 2 is never symlinked into a worktree.** A shared `.lake/packages` looks
> attractive (it saves the download), but it is read-only only by convention, and
> a single consumer running `lake update` mutates the tree for every other
> worktree simultaneously. The download is cheap; a corrupted shared dependency
> tree during a multi-agent session is not. `warm-worktree.sh` therefore fetches
> per worktree, and `worktree-setup.sh` refuses to run `lake update` at all.

Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.

---

## 3. The cache key

```
keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
```

concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.

Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:

1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   need their timestamps preserved.
2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.

---

## 4. On-disk layout

All runtime state lives under `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`, default
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`. Nothing in this tree is ever committed.

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose
├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
└── hot-main/
    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
    │   └── info
    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
    ├── snapshots/
    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    │   │   ├── STAMP
    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
```

Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
calls and no name parsing.

### `STAMP` schema

A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
`eval`ed or `source`d.

```
sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
status=complete|partial
build_seconds=<integer>
toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
warmer_version=1
```

---

## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`

```
local/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]
                          [--targets "<lake targets>"] [--lock-timeout S]
                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]
```

### 5.1 Writer lease

Acquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic
test-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,
`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.

Staleness is decided in this order:

* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead
  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.
* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).

The TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this
repository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,
2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease
mid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to
prevent.

**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that
both judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;
`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and
re-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A
`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.

### 5.2 Build

1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`
   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.
   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and
   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).
3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**
   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and
   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,
   finish, then warm again.
4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply
   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.
   **No `lake update`.**
5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.
   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is
   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent
   prompts may later read.

### 5.3 Atomic publish

The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:

1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).

> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,
> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would
> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real
> trap, not a hypothetical one.

Consumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the
resolved concrete path for the rest of the run.

### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional

If `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and
exits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`
commit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did
compile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say
so loudly.

A non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *"main did not build cleanly"* —
not *"nothing was published."* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a
reason to retry.

### 5.5 Retention

Keep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's
10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never
collected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has
resolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging
directories older than an hour are swept.

## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`

```
local/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]
                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]
```

The consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to
operate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.

Decision procedure:

1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).
2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.
3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.
4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause
   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the
   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.
5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,
   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker
   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,
   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.
   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that
   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.
6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the
   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.

### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule

Re-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:

* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the
  clone;
* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it

# Local Operations Layer — Architecture

This repository is a local-only continuation of the workflow that
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE) evolved on GitHub while
formalizing the low individual degree test (LDT, arXiv:2009.12982). The active
track here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\*=RE
(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).

Every GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local
equivalent that *executes* here. Since 2026-09-01 the issue, PR, evidence and
merge **records** live on GitHub again (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`,
`protocols/issues-prs.md`); what runs is still local. The `.github/` tree is
kept **frozen as reference** — it documents the mechanisms being localized and
is never executed here. The operative layer is this `local/` tree plus the
(already-local) `scripts/` audits and `.githooks/` gates, which port
unchanged.

## Layout

```
local/
├── DESIGN.md          # this file — architecture and invariants
├── README.md          # operator's entry point: commands, lifecycle walkthrough
├── protocols/         # normative protocol documents
│   ├── meta.md        # how protocols evolve; telemetry duties (read first)
│   ├── build-cache.md # hot main cache; no-duplicate-compilation rules
│   ├── ci.md          # local PR CI gate
│   ├── review.md      # reviewer dispatch and gating
│   ├── autofix.md     # auto-fix loop, iteration caps
│   ├── issues-prs.md  # GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle
│   ├── sessions.md    # agent session naming, dispatch, archiving
│   └── EVOLUTION.md   # dated protocol-amendment ledger (research data)
├── personas/          # system prompts for locally dispatched agents
└── bin/               # executables (the workflow engine)
local/briefs/          # per-issue design briefs (committed)
results/telemetry/     # sessions/stages/builds logs, GitHub snapshot (committed)
```

Runtime state that must never be committed lives in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`
(hot cache, snapshots, locks, served site) and `.worktrees/` (gitignored).

## GitHub → local mapping

| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
|---|---|
| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |
| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |
| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |
| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |

## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)

These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.

1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
   unset means enabled.
5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.
6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    command.
11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    exactly as to LDT.

## Naming and identity conventions

- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry
  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy
  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of
  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment
  and the COMMENT review.
- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),
  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub
  issue's.
- **Fix commits**: subjects prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]`
  exactly (the review-gate regex depends on them).
- **Agent sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`. Dispatched
  only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,
  captures the `--json` event stream to
  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.

## Telemetry (research-paper data)

All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.

- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,
  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.
- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.

## Model policy

- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/
  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`).
- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier; Fable-tier is
  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial
  verification).
- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
  reviews its own diff.

 "body": "### Motivation\n\n- Repair the 17 findings from the round-1 review of local issue #0006, published\n  as GitHub issue #4, for the QPBT statement skeleton.\n- Restore the source-facing definitions to the Pauli basis test and its\n  definition closure.  The primary sources are\n  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:231-384,433-502,653-728,832-897,946-1161`,\n  `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57,219-230,258-271`,\n  `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`, and\n  `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391,512-610,908-1225,1426-1447`.\n\n### Description\n\n- Encode `FixedFieldModel` with an actual `ZMod 2` algebra, a basis, its\n  self-duality and normality witnesses, and derive the binary representation\n  from the basis coordinates.  The model is fixed in `AdmissibleParams`, as the\n  paper requires; no fresh field identification is added to `pauli_soundness`.\n- Define `tauObservable` independently from the single-qudit shift and phase\n  operators, retaining the Fourier expansion identities as proof obligations.\n- Correct conditional-linear concatenation, require nonempty graph support,\n  remove the unused low-degree edge set, and provide the proved Magic Square\n  nonemptiness witness.\n- Correct Point/Pair orientation, add both supported Magic Square orientations,\n  make same-type consistency unconditional, and accept unsupported total cases\n  as prescribed by the decider.\n- Use `Matrix.toEuclideanLin` for the shared Hilbert-space action and the\n  state-dependent operator distances; allow the source's `epsilon = 0` boundary.\n- Add the missing helper docstrings and replace stale paper anchors.  Blueprint\n  links are intentionally unchanged in this repair; the known missing `\\\\uses`\n  edges and QPBT chapter links are tracked for the Stage 4.2 synchronization.\n\nAll remaining `sorry`s are proof-level obligations explicitly allowed by the\nStage 4.1 skeleton brief; no definition body or axiom was added.  The fixed\nbasis fields are source-facing data, while the finite serialization equivalence\nand Euclidean coordinate helpers are Lean-only representation infrastructure.\n\n### Statement Integrity\n\n- **Paper assumptions:** admissible `q = 2^k` with odd `k`, `m | q`, a fixed\n  self-dual normal field representation, and a finite-dimensional tensor-product\n  strategy passing the Pauli basis test with probability at least `1 - epsilon`.\n- **Lean assumptions:** `AdmissibleParams` carries `q`, `m`, `d`, the admissibility\n  and divisibility proofs, and the fixed `FixedFieldModel` basis/algebra data;\n  `Strategy` carries finite Euclidean registers and a unit state; the theorem\n  assumes `0 <= epsilon` and the same success inequality.  These are faithful\n  finite-type and boundary hypotheses, not a residual or repair package.\n- **Paper conclusion:** universal constants and a quantitative error scale,\n  local isometries into auxiliary registers tensored with Pauli registers, a\n  unit auxiliary state, and state-dependent closeness of the state and both\n  Pauli POVM families.\n- **Lean conclusion:** existential `a,b` with the stated bounds and a\n  `PauliSoundnessWitness` containing finite auxiliary types, local isometries,\n  and a unit auxiliary vector; it states the Euclidean state inequality and the\n  two explicit squared operator-distance inequalities using `deltaQld`.\n- **Verdict:** faithful finite-dimensional encoding with ordinary typeclass and\n  nonemptiness boundary hypotheses.  No extra bridge, residual, producer, or\n  assumptions bundle is present.  The analytic arguments remain intentional\n  Stage 4.1 proof obligations, and the explicit inequalities make the paper's\n  asymptotic distance convention concrete.\n\n### Testing\n\n- `lake env lean` passed for all twelve edited QPBT modules in dependency order.\n- `git diff --check` and the QPBT line-length audit passed.\n- The proof-hole scan reports only the intentional Stage 4.1 `sorry` sites; no\n  `axiom`, `native_decide`, or kernel-bypass declaration was introduced.\n- The repository pre-commit statement-integrity, proof-debt, faithful-boundary,\n  and conclusion-shaped-hypothesis checks all passed.\n- The direct full build was attempted, but this repair worktree's copied package\n  source cache is incomplete; the authoritative local CI gate is run separately\n  through `local/bin/ci.sh` with the hot cache.\n\n---\nAddresses #4\n",

## Mathlib scouting report — 2026-09-02

### Mathematical source

- MIP\*=RE, `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1415-1877`; blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex`, labels `def:s-w-marginals` through `lem:qld-unitary`.
- Binding interface: `local/briefs/42-ch16-brief.md`, especially the 2026-09-02 adjudication; issue contract: `local/briefs/0019-orchestrator-task.md`.
- The chapter forms side-specific polynomial marginals, decoded Pauli coarse-grainings, pulled-apart observables, and swap unitaries from the global polynomial-pair witness. It states consistency, conjugation, and extraction bounds of order `O(δ_S^(1/4) + md/q)` on the heterogeneous strategy.
- The detached proof of `thm:pauli` is outside issue #19. No earlier scouting report is posted on issue #19.

### Relevant Mathlib definitions

- `Basis.equivFun` — coordinates associated with a basis; suitable for the fixed model's binary-coordinate map (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean:225`).
- `Algebra.leftMulMatrix` — multiplication by a field element in basis coordinates (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ToLin.lean:947`).
- `MvPolynomial.eval` — evaluation used by the bounded polynomial representative (`Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Eval.lean:256`).
- `Matrix.kronecker` — matrix tensor product underlying register placement (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Kronecker.lean:274`).
- `Equiv.prodCongr`, `Equiv.prodComm`, `Equiv.prodAssoc`, `Equiv.prodProdProdComm` — register reindexing equivalences (`Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Prod.lean:73`, `:83`, `:101`, `:107`).

### Relevant Mathlib lemmas and theorems

- `Basis.equivFun_apply`, `Basis.equivFun_self`, `Basis.sum_equivFun` — coordinate evaluation and reconstruction (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean:247`, `:264`, `:255`).
- `Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` — connects algebra trace with the matrix of multiplication (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Defs.lean:87`).
- `Algebra.leftMulMatrix_eq_repr_mul`, `Algebra.leftMulMatrix_mulVec_repr` — coordinate forms of multiplication (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ToLin.lean:965`, `:970`).
- `MvPolynomial.eval_add`, `MvPolynomial.eval_mul`, `MvPolynomial.eval_sum` — algebraic evaluation rules (`Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Eval.lean:286`, `:289`, `:295`).
- `Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul`, `Matrix.kronecker_assoc`, `Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker` — product, reassociation, and adjoint rules for tensor-placed operators (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Kronecker.lean:382`, `:388`, `:408`).
- `Module.finite_of_finite` with `Fintype.ofFinite` — supplies the finite polynomial-answer type; the established local use is in `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersFiniteAnswers.lean:64`.
- No Mathlib theorem directly supplies the QPBT pulled-apart measurements, twisted commutation estimate, swap conjugation, or extraction witness.

### Relevant MIPStarRE declarations

Already present in the Stage 4.1 source:

- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.FixedFieldModel` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.AdmissibleParams.model` — fixed field, basis dimension, basis, self-duality, and normality (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean:40`; `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/PauliBasisTest.lean:58`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliScalar`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.PauliRegister` — scalar and register types (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean:84`, `:118`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.phaseSign`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauliProj`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.tauObservable` — Pauli phase, projectors, and observables (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Pauli.lean:43`, `:86`, `:94`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Cube`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEncoding`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.lowDegreeEnc`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.indicatorVec` — low-degree encoding API (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean:30`, `:49`, `:59`, `:68`).
- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess` and `postprocess_effect` — exact basis for polynomial marginals and finite coarse-graining (`MIPStarRE/Quantum/Measurement.lean:127`, `:136`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Game`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Strategy` — the strategy already has distinct `ιA`, `ιB`, `A`, and `B`; `heteroKron` and `applyOperatorToState` support heterogeneous placement (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Defs.lean:32`, `:88`, `:108`, `:117`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.opFamilyDistSq` — state-dependent operator-family distance (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Distance.lean:39`).
- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaQld` — existing soundness error functional (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Soundness.lean:34`).

Required from issue #16:

- `FixedFieldModel.binaryCoordinates`, with the canonical trace/dot-coordinate specializations, in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/SelfDualBasis.lean`.
- `boolToScalar`, `cubeEmbed`, `decodeAt`, `decodeBool`, and `decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc` in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems.lean`.
- The bounded `polyFunc` `Fintype` instance in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`.
- `Strategy.IsProjective`, `consistencyDefect`, `IsConsistentWithin`, `opDistSq`, its `Unit` bridge, and the neutral state operations `conjIsometry`, `reindexState`, `isometryTensor`, `vecTensor`, and `prodShuffle`.
- The final names for full-field decoding, `IsEncoding`, and the restricted decoding/dot-product identity are not yet frozen. Chapter 16 must bind to the landed declarations rather than introduce replacements.

Required from issue #17:

- A heterogeneous `ProjectiveSetting P ε`, its expanded six-register state, and explicit side-indexed placement maps.
- Side-specific typed and raw point/Pauli measurements derived from the original `A` and `B` strategy families.
- `exists_projective_padded_strategy`.
- The adjudication supersedes the earlier shared-space sketch. Exact accessor names are not yet available because issue #17 has no implementation or PR.

Required from issue #18:

- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Poly`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyPair`.
- An unguarded `GlobalPairWitness` and `exists_globalPairWitness`, with projective polynomial-pair measurements for both heterogeneous sides and no symmetry or divisibility assumption.
- `deltaQld_mono`.
- The final side-indexed measurement fields are not frozen. A witness exposing only one shared `Smeas` would not satisfy chapter 16.

All four involved branches currently point to `b5da371`; issues #16–#18 have no commits or PRs. PR #5 is open at `46e32d6`, cleanly mergeable into `main`, and contains the Stage 4.1 base.

### Suggested approach

Wait for PR #5 and issues #16–#18 to land. Rebase issue #19 onto the resulting `main`, inspect the serialized declarations, and implement against those exact interfaces. Do not recreate `ProjectiveSetting`, `GlobalPairWitness`, polynomial carriers, decoding, binary coordinates, distances, or state operations.

Use `Measurement.postprocess` for both side-specific polynomial marginals; use the landed full-field decoder with an explicit `IsEncoding` hypothesis; reuse `phaseSign`, `tauObservable`, and `P.model` directly. Define only the chapter-owned finite coarse-graining, pulled-apart operators, swap operators, and extraction witness. The corrected cross-basis phase statement needs its required `**Local fix:**` paper-gap citation.

Rebase/build order:

1. Merge PR #5.
2. Merge #16 and verify its algebra, distance, strategy-class, and state modules compile.
3. Rebase and merge #17; verify genuinely heterogeneous placements and side accessors.
4. Rebase and merge #18; verify `PolyPair P`, both side measurements, and the unguarded witness.
5. Rebase #19; reconcile the single serialized `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` import list without dropping sibling imports.
6. Compile `Extraction/Defs.lean`, then `Observables.lean` and `Consistency.lean`, then `Unitary.lean`.
7. Run the prescribed proof-hole scan, `lake build`, blueprint build, declaration checker, CI, and independent review.

Reject stale interface names such as `ExpandedSetting`, a shared `S.ι`, singular shared measurements, `[FieldModel P.q]`, `SelfDualNormalBasis`, or `Distribution.dirac`; the binding versions are heterogeneous `ProjectiveSetting`, `P.model`, side-indexed measurements, and `uniformDistribution Unit`.

### Gaps to fill

- No issue #16, #17, or #18 implementation exists in the checked branches, so their final serialized field/accessor names cannot yet be cited.
- The current worktree has 12 QPBT `.lean` files but no QPBT `.olean` files. `FieldBasis.lean` and `LowDegreeCode.lean` check independently; `Pauli.lean` currently fails because `Algebra/FieldBasis.olean` is absent.
- The hot cache is complete for its recorded snapshot but predates QPBT and contains only Quantum/LDT objects. After rebasing, use the normal locked build/cache workflow; do not copy `.olean` files between sibling worktrees.
- The landed upstream APIs must settle two contracts before extraction can type-check: canonical full-field decoding names and the exact side-indexed `ProjectiveSetting`/`GlobalPairWitness` accessors.
- The chapter-specific consistency, twisted-commutation, swap-conjugation, and extraction statements are genuinely absent from both Mathlib and the current project. They must remain named chapter 16 proof obligations, not assumptions added to an upstream witness.
- Paper-gap documentation remains required for the decoding restriction, corrected cross-phase calculation, and the unitary/state-transfer step owned by Stage 4.3.

Inspected issues #16–#19 and PR #5; `local/briefs/42-ch16-brief.md`; the issue #19 task brief; paper lines 1415–1877; the complete chapter 16 blueprint; `docs/api_surface.md`; relevant `audits/`; all current QPBT and Quantum sources; sibling branches and worktrees; build-cache metadata and `.olean` inventory. Searched Mathlib by basis coordinates, algebra trace, multiplication matrices, multivariate evaluation, Kronecker products, product equivalences, finite modules, measurement coarse-graining, operator distance, Pauli observables, and extraction terminology.
